meta.description: Branson made the joke at the Airbus A380 rollout in January 2005 — but Reuters recorded different words. The polished version circulating online is unsourced.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'With the casino and the beds, our passengers will have at least two ways to get lucky on one of our flights'?
meta.ogDescription: Branson's joke is real; this wording isn't. Reuters recorded a looser line at the 2005 A380 rollout. Wikiquote files the polished version as unsourced.

answer.label: Not Branson’s wording — a tidied-up paraphrase
answer.authorDates: Born 1950 · British entrepreneur, founder of Virgin Atlantic
answer.sourceLine: Branson really did make this joke — at the Airbus A380 rollout in Toulouse on 18 January 2005, where Virgin Atlantic set out plans for an in-flight casino and 35 private double beds. But the Reuters reporters in the room recorded something looser and hedged: “Since you have gaming and you have private double beds maybe there are two ways of getting lucky on a Virgin plane.” The polished corporate version above — first person, “our passengers,” “at least two ways” — has never been traced to any source, and Wikiquote keeps it off Branson’s page for exactly that reason.

source.excerpt: Gyms, beauty parlours, private double beds and an in-flight casino will feature on Virgin Atlantic’s giant Airbus A380 planes when it starts flying them in three years’ time, the airline’s half-owner Richard Branson said. “Since you have gaming and you have private double beds maybe there are two ways of getting lucky on a Virgin plane,” entrepreneur Branson told reporters in France.
trail: Wikiquote keeps this line off Richard Branson’s article entirely — it sits in the “Unsourced” list on the talk page ↗, under a notice that Wikiquote no longer allows unsourced quotations, and it is absent from the sourced quotes on his main page ↗.

A Reuters report filed at the Airbus A380 rollout in Toulouse quotes Branson making the joke in different words: “Since you have gaming and you have private double beds maybe there are two ways of getting lucky on a Virgin plane” ↗. The same wire text survives in an archived MSNBC page datelined Toulouse ↗, carrying a Reuters copyright line.

The polished version travels with nothing attached: AZQuotes prints it under Branson’s name and cites no source whatsoever ↗. No book, transcript, interview or Virgin press release carrying this wording has been located.
The plans behind the joke never flew — Virgin Atlantic’s six-aircraft A380 order was deferred repeatedly and cancelled in March 2018 ↗, so no passenger ever boarded the casino cabin being described.
source.excerptNote: This is the documented remark, not the version that circulates. Note the hedge — “maybe there are two ways” — which the popular rewrite removes.

The remark it derives from was spoken in 2005 and reported by Reuters; that wire report is a modern, in-copyright work, so the excerpt above is reproduced here as a short quotation for the purpose of attribution and comment.

author.bio: Richard Branson, born 18 July 1950, is the English founder of the Virgin Group, which he expanded from a record label into airlines, rail, telecoms and spaceflight. He founded Virgin Atlantic in 1984 and built much of its brand on exactly this register — a slightly cheeky one-liner delivered to reporters, usually while announcing something extravagant. He is also one of the internet’s most-quoted businesspeople, which means a large share of the lines circulating under his name have been smoothed, shortened or invented outright.

cite.sourceCitation: “Virgin eyes gyms, casino, double beds on A380 jet.” Reuters, 18–19 January 2005, filed from Toulouse, France (as published by China Daily, 18 January 2005, and MSNBC, 19 January 2005). Branson’s reported wording: “Since you have gaming and you have private double beds maybe there are two ways of getting lucky on a Virgin plane.” The circulating “With the casino and the beds…” wording is unsourced and is held on Wikiquote’s talk page under “Unsourced.”

misattribution.heading: Why this wording keeps travelling
misattribution.intro: Nothing here is a fabrication out of thin air — Branson made the joke, in public, in front of reporters. What has gone wrong is narrower and more common: the sentence in circulation is a rewrite that no source records, passed hand to hand until it looked like a quotation.

items.why: AZQuotes prints the line under Branson’s name with no book, date, interview or occasion attached ↗ — just the words and the byline. That bare format is how the polished version spread.
The line does not appear on Branson’s Wikiquote page ↗. It sits instead in the “Unsourced” section of the talk page ↗, beneath a notice that Wikiquote no longer allows unsourced quotations.

Recounting the same 2005 announcement, Simple Flying renders the gag as “two chances to get lucky” ↗ — a third wording again. When secondary accounts of one remark diverge like this, none of them is the quotation.

misattribution.truthLine: The only wording with a contemporaneous source behind it is the one Reuters filed from Toulouse on 18 January 2005 ↗: “Since you have gaming and you have private double beds maybe there are two ways of getting lucky on a Virgin plane.”

context.heading: The plane that never flew, and the joke that outlived it
lead: On 18 January 2005 Airbus rolled the A380 superjumbo out in Toulouse, and Richard Branson used the occasion to describe what Virgin Atlantic intended to put inside its six of them: a gym, beauty parlours, a gambling area with blackjack and roulette open to economy and business passengers, and 35 private double beds per aircraft. Asked about it, he made the obvious joke — and Reuters wrote it down.

Virgin Atlantic never took delivery. The order was deferred repeatedly and finally cancelled in March 2018, with the deposits rolled into A330 and A350 orders. The casino, the beauty parlour and the double beds were never built. The one-liner, meanwhile, kept flying — and somewhere along the way it got rewritten into a cleaner, more quotable sentence than the one Branson actually said.
detailsBody: The reported remark is conversational and hedged: “Since you have gaming and you have private double beds maybe there are two ways of getting lucky on a Virgin plane.” The circulating version drops the hedge, converts it to corporate first person (“our passengers,” “one of our flights”), swaps “gaming” for “the casino,” and firms “maybe there are two ways” into “will have at least two ways.”

Each change makes the line punchier and more printable, which is precisely how quotations drift on their way into aggregator databases. None of the changes is documented in any source, and no book, interview transcript or press release carrying the polished wording has been located.
context.pull: The aircraft was cancelled. The joke was rewritten. Only the joke is still in circulation.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote holds "With the casino and the beds, our passengers will have at least two ways to get lucky on one of our flights" in a section literally headed "Unsourced", beneath a notice that Wikiquote no longer allows unsourced quotations and they are being removed from articles.
Richard Branson's main Wikiquote page (its sourced Quotes section) does not contain the casino-and-beds line.

A wire report dated 18 January 2005 quotes Branson: "Since you have gaming and you have private double beds maybe there are two ways of getting lucky on a Virgin plane," said while announcing Virgin's A380 plans ahead of the aircraft's unveiling that Tuesday in Toulouse, France, including a gym, a gambling area with blackjack and roulette, and 35 private double beds per aircraft.

The archived MSNBC page carries the same Reuters text, updated 10:55 a.m. ET Jan. 19, 2005, with a TOULOUSE, France dateline, the same Branson quotation, and the closing line "Copyright 2005 Reuters Limited."
AZQuotes displays the exact circulating wording attributed to Richard Branson with no source of any kind — no book, year, page, interview or occasion.

Simple Flying's retrospective on Virgin Atlantic's A380 cabin plans renders Branson's 2005 gag as passengers having "two chances to get lucky", crediting The Guardian (2005), and reports the casino/gym/double-bed plans and a 2007 Bloomberg interview about bars, showers, roulette and blackjack.

Virgin Atlantic ordered six Airbus A380-800s with options on a further six, delivery initially due in 2006 but repeatedly deferred; the order was officially cancelled in March 2018, with deposits transferred to A330 and A350 orders.
Richard Branson was born 18 July 1950, is English, and founded Virgin Atlantic in 1984.
